text:
Tropical Storm Warning issued for all of South Carolina
COLUMBIA, SC (WACH) — Helene strengthened to a Category 1 hurricane Wednesday morning and is forecast to strengthen to a major hurricane by Thursday.
The forecast track takes Helene inland across Georgia Thursday night, weakening a tropical storm by Friday morning.
Due to the expected impacts from Helene, a Tropical Storm Warning has been issued for the entire state of South Carolina.
Showers will begin early Thursday mainly in the western Midlands and near the Central Savannah River Area.
Rain will likely become more widespread across the Midlands Thursday afternoon.
The worst of the rain will likely move through the Midlands between midnight and 8 am Friday.
Up to 5" will be possible in the western Midlands which could result in flash flooding and river flooding.
Winds are forecast to be strongest Thursday evening through Friday morning for the Midlands.
Tropical storm conditions (sustained winds at or above 39 mph) will be most likely southwest of I-26.
Wind gusts up to 60 mph will be possible in the southwest Midlands, and could be up to 50 mph for Columbia.
This wind combined with the saturated soil could be enough to down trees and power lines, likely resulting in some power outages.
South Carolina will also be vulnerable to tornadoes Thursday night and early Friday, particularly from the southern Midlands to the Low Country.
